body.heading: Everything has a name
paragraphs: Look around you. Everything you can point at has a name: cat, ball, teacher, tree. Words that name things are called nouns — but you can just call them naming words.
Naming words come in three families. Let's meet them!

body.heading: People
paragraphs: teacher, baby, farmer, sister, doctor, friend.
If you can hug them or wave to them, their name is a naming word for a person.

body.heading: Places
paragraphs: school, garden, beach, kitchen, park, library.
If you can go there, its name is a naming word for a place.

body.heading: Things
paragraphs: ball, book, apple, chair, rainbow, shoe.
If you can hold it, see it or point to it, its name is a naming word for a thing.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Play 'I spy a naming word': 'I spy a thing that is red.' Take turns guessing.
2. How many naming words can your family shout out in thirty seconds? Sort them into people, places and things.

takeaway: Naming words (nouns) name people, places and things — and you can point at almost all of them.
